title: CRUD with JSON Server
summary: Spin up a fake REST API and do the four CRUD operations against it.
heading: CRUD with JSON Server

blocks.text: To practice talking to an API you need a server. JSON Server turns a plain JSON file into a full REST API in seconds — no backend code needed. It's perfect for learning and prototypes.
Create a db.json file with some starting data. Each top-level key becomes a resource (a collection).

blocks.label: Terminal
blocks.code:
json-server --watch db.json
# API now running at http://localhost:3000

blocks.text: You instantly get the endpoints /users and /users/:id — and JSON Server saves every change back into db.json.
CRUD stands for the four things you do with data: Create, Read, Update, and Delete. Every app — a todo list, a shop, a social feed — is mostly CRUD underneath.
Over a REST API (Chapter 33), each CRUD operation is a different HTTP method.

blocks.label: Revisit Chapter 33: REST APIs In Depth

blocks.text: Reading has two shapes: get the whole collection, or get one item by its id. These are plain GET requests — you can even open the URLs in your browser.
On the command line you can try it with curl:
Send a new item in the request body to the collection. JSON Server gives it a new id and saves it, then returns the created item.
Point at one item's id and send the full updated object. JSON Server replaces it and returns the new version.
Point at the item's id with the DELETE method. JSON Server removes it and returns an empty object.
Check db.json after each call — you'll see the file actually change as you create, update, and delete.
A real collection can hold thousands of rows — you never load them all at once. Pagination fetches one page at a time: ask for a page number and a page size, and the server returns just that slice.
JSON Server paginates with the _page and _limit query parameters.

blocks.label: requests
blocks.code:
GET /users?_page=1&_limit=10   # items 1–10
GET /users?_page=2&_limit=10   # items 11–20
GET /users?_page=3&_limit=10   # items 21–30

blocks.text: Version note: JSON Server v1 uses _per_page instead of _limit and returns a wrapper object — { first, prev, next, last, pages, data } — with the page in data. Older v0 uses _limit + the X-Total-Count header shown above.
HttpClient hides headers by default. Pass { observe: 'response' } to get the full response, then read X-Total-Count from res.headers.

blocks.label: users.ts

blocks.text: Pagination usually pairs with sorting and filtering — all just query parameters in JSON Server.

blocks.label: examples
blocks.code:
GET /users?_sort=age&_order=desc   # sort by age, high → low
GET /users?city=Delhi              # only users in Delhi
GET /users?age_gte=18&age_lte=30   # age between 18 and 30
GET /users?q=asha                  # full-text search

blocks.text: Combine them freely: /users?city=Delhi&_sort=age&_page=1&_limit=10 — filter, sort, then page.

items: JSON Server turns a db.json into a real REST API for practice.
JSON Server saves changes straight into db.json.
